definitions.explanation: A traditional form of Japanese poetry consisting of 17 morae (sound units) in a 5-7-5 pattern. Haiku typically focus on nature and seasonal imagery.

examples.japanese: {松尾芭蕉|まつおばしょう}は{日本|にほん}で{最|もっと}も{有名|ゆうめい}な{俳句|はいく}{詩人|しじん}だ。
examples.english: Matsuo Basho is the most famous haiku poet in Japan.

examples.japanese: {俳句|はいく}には{季語|きご}を{入|い}れるのが{基本|きほん}です。
examples.english: The basic rule is to include a seasonal word in haiku.

examples.japanese: {学校|がっこう}の{授業|じゅぎょう}で{俳句|はいく}を{作|つく}った。
examples.english: I wrote haiku in school class.

notes:
{俳句|はいく} is a traditional Japanese poetry form with strict structural requirements:
- 17 morae in 5-7-5 pattern
- Contains a {季語|きご} (seasonal reference word)
- Often includes a {切|き}れ{字|じ} (cutting word) for pause or emphasis

Famous haiku poets ({俳人|はいじん}):
- {松尾芭蕉|まつおばしょう} (Matsuo Basho)
- {与謝蕪村|よさぶそん} (Yosa Buson)
- {小林一茶|こばやしいっさ} (Kobayashi Issa)

Related terms:
- {俳人|はいじん} (haiku poet)
- {季語|きご} (seasonal word)
- {川柳|せんりゅう} (senryu - similar form but focuses on human nature rather than seasons)
